newsitem.title: UK: Carib 50,000 tonne tankers slump, Mideast flat.
newsitem.headline: Carib 50,000 tonne tankers slump, Mideast flat.

text.p: Very large crude carrier (VLCC) rates from West Africa to the U.S. showed a firmer tone on Wednesday while from the Middle East they were steady in a dull market, brokers said.
Few sectors showed much change in rates, apart from 70,000 tonnes Caribs/upcoast, which slumped to W117.5 from W135.
"There are around 10 ships available over the next few days. The next fixture will be at W115," a U.S. broker said.
Modern VLCCs on West Africa/U.S. trips were assessed at W70, up about 2.5 points, on a shortage of tonnage, another said.
But the 130,000 tonne West Africa market showed little sign of life, remaining at around W90.
The key Middle East sector was quiet, still feeling the after-effects of the Chinese new year and of Moslem holidays. VLCC rates were unchanged at W50 to the west, W65 to Japan and W50 to Singapore.
"Volume seems to have dried up for the moment," one broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 vessels edged up to W97.5 on good activity with some 11 vessels fixed, another said.
The Mediterranean was inactive, with 80,000 tonne vessels steady at W120-125, while 130,000 tonners slipped to W87.5-90 from W92.5 on low enquiry levels, he added.
Fuel oil was steady with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W210 and cross-Med around W180. In Caribs/USAC 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes edged up to W175 from W170.
